mission_title: Robot: slow, high-res model and texture
goal: A free (local) 3D model of the reference robot with its native PBR texture, sharper than the first mission. Its best round (r18: trellis2, robot_ref, seed 51951, shape_cfg 3.75, structure_cfg 8.0, tex_cfg 1.75, at 1024 voxels, 12 steps, remesh 768 with 20 smoothing passes) got 10/10 from the reviewer, but Patrik judges it not good enough: the face and small details are soft. This mission spends more time per model (higher voxel resolution, more steps, less smoothing) to get crisper shape and texture. Rounds are slow on the 8 GB T1000; 1536 may run out of memory. Two GPUs run rounds side by side, each its own chain: the T1000 (int8, faster) and the Quadro M4000 (fp32, about 1.6x slower). Time per round on the T1000: about 15 min at resolution 1024, about 3 h at 1536 with 28 steps; the M4000 takes about 1.6x as long. Prefer 1280 or fewer steps when a lever change is a small experiment, and save 1536 for promising settings.

model.help: Image-to-3D model. pixal3d (TRELLIS.2 fine-tune, sharper projection of the image) or trellis2 (Microsoft base model).

image.help: Input image. robot_ref: the original reference (front, full body). id_front: a Krea-2 identity front view of the same robot, cleaner light.

seed.help: Random seed for structure, shape and texture sampling.

shape_cfg.help: Guidance of the detailed shape stage. Lower: smoother, fewer artifacts (3.5 gave the cleanest pelvis before). Higher: follows the image harder.

structure_cfg.help: Guidance of the coarse structure (overall silhouette, limbs separated or fused).

tex_cfg.help: Guidance of the texture stage. 1 is the default; higher can sharpen colors but may add noise.

resolution.help: Voxel resolution of the high-res shape and texture stages. Texture colors are baked from the voxels, so this sets how many samples a face gets (1024 = old setting, 1536 = TRELLIS.2/Pixal3D standard quality). Higher is slower and needs more VRAM.

steps.help: Sampling steps for structure, high-res shape and texture (the low-res shape stage gets 8 more). Old setting 12; 25-40 is slower but sharper.

remesh.help: Resolution of the final remesh before texturing. Old setting 768; higher keeps more small shape detail (face, fingers).

smooth.help: Smoothing passes in the remesh. Old setting 20, which rounds off small shapes such as the face; 0-5 keeps them.

moves: Round 1 repeats the first mission's best levers (r18) at high quality: compare its review with r18's to see what the slow settings bring.
Out of memory or a crash at resolution 1536: go to 1408 or 1280; if that fails too, 1024 with more steps.
Soft or smeared face: raise resolution, lower smooth toward 0, raise remesh.
Faceted, noisy or bumpy surface: raise smooth to 6-10 or lower shape_cfg.
Steps above 30 rarely help much: only go higher when the texture looks noisy.
Fused or blobby limbs: raise structure_cfg a little or try another seed.
A good result: keep its levers, try one nearby seed and the other model (pixal3d) with the same quality settings.

The M4000 is a support card (slower, fp32), capped at resolution 1024 and 20 steps (about 25 min a round): use it for quick seed, model and cfg exploration, and give the T1000 the 1536 rounds for the most promising settings.

steps.label: Review: model and texture
criteria: The model and texture belong to the same robot as the reference: white armor plates, dark joints, small red accents.

Be strict about sharpness: the face, eyes, panel lines and fingers must be crisp, as on a hand-made game asset. Any softness, smear or blurred patch costs points; 10/10 only if nothing could be sharper.
Separated, well-formed limbs and hands that would rig and deform well; no lumps, holes or noisy surface.
